description: A four-panel composite figure in which every panel plots one mechanical property against the square root of the average κ-carbide size, d_Car^0.5, for solution-processed Fe–Mn–Al–C low-density steels. (a) plots R_p0.2 and R_m (MPa, ordinate 0–1500) versus d_Car^0.5 (abscissa 0–10): black squares are tensile strength and red circles yield strength, with two dashed linear fits annotated R_m = 786 + 54.6 d_Car^0.5 and R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5. The black tensile-strength points stay between the 800 and 1200 gridlines and rise only gently, whereas the red yield-strength points climb steeply from the 450–500 level at d = 0 towards the 1100 gridline near d_Car^0.5 ≈ 7, so the two lines converge at large d_Car^0.5. (b) plots A_5, total tensile elongation (%, 0–80), falling linearly, annotated A_5 = 64.5 − 6.445 d_Car^0.5. (c) plots Z, area reduction (%, 0–100), also decreasing linearly, annotated Z = 78 − 3.85 d_Car^0.5. (d) plots Charpy impact toughness AkV at −40 °C (J, 0–500) versus d_Car^0.5 (0–5); its dashed fit covers only d_Car^0.5 < 2, beyond which the data lie at the near-zero level. The group therefore shows strengths rising while elongation, area reduction and impact toughness all fall as κ-carbides coarsen.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend identifies the black squares as Tensile strength and the red circles as Yield strength, both plotted against d_Car^0.5.
Panel (a) prints two linear fits: R_m = 786 + 54.6 d_Car^0.5 (tensile strength) and R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5 (yield strength), showing a steeper slope for yield strength.
Panel (b) prints A_5 = 64.5 − 6.445 d_Car^0.5, i.e. total tensile elongation decreases linearly with d_Car^0.5.
Panel (c) prints Z = 78 − 3.85 d_Car^0.5, i.e. area reduction decreases linearly with d_Car^0.5.
In panel (d) the dashed linear fit is drawn only for d_Car^0.5 < 2; data points beyond d_Car^0.5 ≈ 2 lie at the near-zero level of the ordinate (0–500 J scale).

The caption states that all four panels plot properties against d_Car^0.5 for low-density steels with different alloying elements, and that dashed lines are linear fits (in (d) only for d_Car^0.5 < 2).
The citing text reports a constant slope of 97.1 MPa/nm^1/2 from the yield-strength versus square-root κ-carbide size fitting, implying strong shear hardening from κ-carbides.
The citing text estimates the flow stress in the absence of any κ-carbide strengthening contribution as about 478 MPa, attributed to solid-solution hardening and austenite grain-size strengthening.
The citing text claims particle-shear strengthening remains active for κ-carbide sizes as large as 50 nm, much larger than the typical ~5 nm critical size for the shearing-to-Orowan transition.
The citing text reports that only three designed low-density steels had high impact toughness: Fe30Mn6Al1.0C (354 J), Fe30Mn8Al1.0C (294 J) and Fe30Mn10Al1.0C (237 J).
The citing text interprets elongation (b) and area reduction (c) as both decreasing linearly with the square root of the κ-carbide diameter.
The citing text notes that in Fig. 7(a) tensile strength and yield strength values become similar at large κ-carbide sizes, which variations in κ-carbide size alone cannot explain.

sample_hints: low-density steels with different alloying elements

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of R_p0.2 and R_m (MPa, 0–1500) versus d_Car^0.5 (0–10). Legend: black squares = Tensile strength, red circles = Yield strength. Dashed linear fits annotated R_m = 786 + 54.6 d_Car^0.5 (black) and R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5 (red). Tensile-strength points are nearly flat; yield-strength points rise strongly, converging with the tensile line at large d_Car^0.5.

A_5, total tensile elongation (%, 0–80) versus d_Car^0.5 (0–10) for black square data points. Dashed decreasing linear fit annotated A_5 = 64.5 − 6.445 d_Car^0.5, extrapolating to near zero elongation at d_Car^0.5 ≈ 10.

Z, area reduction (%, 0–100) versus d_Car^0.5 (0–10) for black round data points clustered at low d_Car^0.5 with one isolated point near d_Car^0.5 ≈ 7. Dashed decreasing linear fit annotated Z = 78 − 3.85 d_Car^0.5.

Charpy impact toughness AkV at −40 °C (J, 0–500) versus d_Car^0.5 (0–5) for black square points. A dashed line is fitted only over d_Car^0.5 < 2, dropping from about the 350 J level at d = 0 to zero near d_Car^0.5 ≈ 2; data points at d_Car^0.5 ≈ 4–5 lie essentially at 0 J.
